chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abi al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: “When the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was brought one who drank wine, he would strike him. If he was brought a second time, he would strike him. If he was brought a third time, he struck his neck.” I said: And nabidh? He said: “If its drinker is seized while he has become intoxicated, he is struck eighty lashes.” I said: What do you say if he is seized for it a second time? He said: “I strike him.” I said: Then if he is seized for it a third time? He said: “He is killed just as the drinker of wine is killed.” I said: What do you say if the drinker of nabidh is seized and he has not become intoxicated—should he be flogged? He said: “No.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this report contains regarding the distinction between nabidh and wine, and that flogging is not carried out for it except when intoxication occurs, is to be understood as a form of taqiyyah, because that is the view of the jurists of some of the generality. For we have already clarified that there is no distinction between wine and nabidh in its small amount or large amount, and that it necessitates the hadd. The same ruling applies to what he narrated:

key_terms.شَارِبِ ٱلْخَمْرِ: the one who drinks wine or intoxicating liquor
key_terms.ضُرِبَ ثَمَانِينَ: he was struck with eighty lashes as the prescribed punishment
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: he is killed, referring here to punishment upon repeated offense
key_terms.ٱلتَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection, used here to explain the report’s wording
key_terms.ٱلنَّبِيذُ: nabidh, an intoxicating drink discussed in legal rulings
key_terms.ٱلْحَدَّ: the prescribed legal punishment in sacred law

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about the hadd for drinking wine and nabidh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal punishment for drinking intoxicants, mentioning repeated offenses for wine and nabidh. The compiler then states that the reported distinction between nabidh and wine is to be understood under taqiyyah, affirming that both are treated alike in the obligation of hadd.
